profile_scope: OpenVINO synchronous CPU FP32 inference only; preprocessing and postprocessing excluded.

dominant_compute_interpretation.primary: Vision-backbone convolution family, especially early high-spatial-resolution convolutions.
dominant_compute_interpretation.secondary: Transformer fully-connected execution family over tensors including [302,1,512].
dominant_compute_interpretation.conclusion: The CPU bottleneck is distributed across repeated convolution and fully-connected compute rather than one pathological operation.

interpretation_limits: Profiling overhead means these latency percentiles do not replace the formal benchmark.
Operation times may overlap or execute in parallel, so their sum is not a general end-to-end formula.
Runtime fusion can make a reported node represent multiple graph operations.
This profile cannot localize preprocessing, postprocessing, robot I/O, queues or system safety paths because they are outside the measured scope.
The result applies to CPU FP32 on this frozen input and model; it is not automatically the GPU bottleneck ranking.

demonstrated_understanding: The convolution family remains the primary cost even if the single slowest node is removed, because that node accounts for only about 3.9% of the profiled sum.
Profiling instrumentation adds observation overhead and therefore does not replace the formal latency benchmark.
Different devices require separate profiling because plugins, kernels, operator support, fusion, scheduling and memory behavior differ.
The observed CPU bottleneck is dispersed across many convolution and fully-connected nodes rather than caused by one unique node.
